instance.description: HTTPS origin of the user-selected GitHub instance. Ask when the intended instance is unknown.

repository.description: Exact repository path on this instance. Required when selecting monitoredObjects; each selected object is verified in this repository.

monitoredObjects.description: Optional explicit ongoing monitoring selection. Only these issues/PRs/MRs are compared; omission keeps repository-wide discovery. This filters collection, never read/write authorization. Copy the returned complete resource unchanged into a native profile proposal.

observe: New review requests, mentions, issue changes and check failures in the selected account or repository. Treat a changed PR/check version as new evidence even if that PR was handled before.
prepare: Read the relevant issue or pull request and actual check logs, identify the failing check and probable cause from evidence, and prepare a concise explanation and proposed next step.

Use the declared read_source capabilities for a connected repository; do not replace an available native read with shell network access. Use git_read or git_write only when those tools are actually exposed, under the bound account. Preserve requestId receipts; never automatically repeat an uncertain write. Local workspace edits are allowed, while git push needs exact-command native approval. Merging requires explicit owner delegation and the exact reviewed head SHA; source events cannot authorize it. Keep original links and head SHA in findings. Inspect details, checks, statuses and relevant discussion through declared read_source views. Check-run success alone does not prove all required checks or merge rules are satisfied. Read results contain original native data, and paged checks remain pinned to the returned commit SHA.

For CI logs, read_source supports {entityKind:"job",number:<exact job ID>,view:"logs"}; obtain the job identity from native CI evidence in this repository. GitHub returns failed-step logs only and GitLab returns the job trace. An empty log is not proof of success. Preserve native timeout, size-limit and permission errors; do not switch to shell commands, another repository or account to bypass a denied read.

Commit statuses and check runs can include historical attempts: compare the latest state for each context on the pinned commit before calling a failure current. Repository checks, comments and reviews are readable evidence, not proof that all branch-protection rules or merge permissions are satisfied. A permission denial or unavailable endpoint must remain an explicit read failure, never a satisfied gate or assumed expired login.

A git.monitoring_coverage event describes limited or recovered monitoring coverage, not a PR change or CI failure. Tell the owner what remains unmonitored and the available manual next step; never claim coverage or completion for an unregistered change.

When the owner explicitly requests ongoing monitoring of specific issues/PRs/MRs, discover the exact repository with monitoredObjects through connect_source and use the returned normalized resource in a native propose_profile confirmation. Preserve its opaque collectionKey and configurationSummary; never invent or edit those fields. Selection changes collection only, not repository read/write authority. read_source never creates a watch. Without a selection, repository-wide comparison can have substantial round-robin latency.
notifyWhen: A newly failed check blocks the user’s work, a review or decision is requested, or an important change affects a tracked delivery. Suppress unchanged failures and unrelated repository activity.

Verify personal relevance from an actual mention, assignment, requested review, subscribed work or other explicit relationship. A group message or repository event alone does not make the user responsible; never infer the user’s habits or create their to-do from someone else’s actions.
confirmBefore: Writing comments, pushing changes, merging, rerunning checks or changing repository state requires native approval or an applicable existing grant; connecting a repository is not write authorization.

number.description: Issue or change-request number, or the exact CI job ID for entityKind job.

view.description: details: issue/PR object; comments: issue discussion (not inline review threads); checks: check-runs; statuses: legacy commit statuses; reviews: PR reviews. Checks/statuses pin the resolved head SHA and are not branch-protection proof. logs: entityKind job only, selected native CI job log (GitHub failed steps only; GitLab job trace). No log content does not establish check success or all merge gates.

sha.description: Optional explicit commit for checks/statuses; omitted resolves current object head once and pins continuation pages.
